title: Incident Replay & Evidence Bundle PRD (draft)
body:
Purpose and motivation:

This doc captures a product requirement draft for an Incident Replay / Evidence Bundle feature for Private deployments (customer-managed networking, VPC, on-prem). The feature helps customers and Redwood operators reconstruct, validate, and export a tamper-evident set of artifacts that explain a network or configuration incident tied to approval-gate decisions and audit logs.

Why we need it (short):
- Customers operating in regulated environments need a compact, queryable, and exportable representation of what changed, who approved it, and what telemetry proves the system behaved as expected.
- Operators need fast triage: surface the chain-of-actions, produce a minimally-sufficient evidence package for compliance teams, and optionally replay the sequence in a safe sandbox.
- Current private-deploy audit artifacts are fragmented across control-plane logs, customer syslog exports, and approval decision records; stitching is manual and slow.

Goals (measurable):
- Provide a standard evidence bundle format that contains the minimal artifacts to show: what change was requested, the approval decision path, the time-series of observed network/agent telemetry, and cryptographic attestations linking records.
- Enable a one-click export from Console (or an API) that produces a signed, compressed evidence bundle within 10s for typical incidents (<1000 events).
- Add an "Incident Replay" view in Console that sequences events and approval steps with time-aligned telemetry; initial intent is read-only sandboxed replay (no live apply).
- Define retention and access controls so evidence bundles can be generated for events within the retention window and only by authorized roles.

Out of scope (for this draft):
- Live rollback automation.
- Deep packet capture replay.
- Full SIEM integration beyond syslog/forwarding.

User personas and stories:

- Platform security engineer (customer): "When a production tenant reports a connectivity regression after a VPC change, I want to quickly export proof that shows which firewall rule changed, who approved it, and the observed route table change, so I can send to internal audit."

- Redwood SRE on-call: "I need to see the approval gate trace and the last 60 minutes of control-plane telemetry aligned with the change so I can understand whether an operator action or configuration drift caused the incident."

- Compliance manager: "I need a signed artifact bundle that can be archived off-site for 7 years in major regulated customers; the bundle must be small and verifiable."

Core concepts and definitions:

- Evidence bundle: A compressed, signed package (.reb - Redwood Evidence Bundle) containing a small set of files: event_manifest.json (index), audit_log.ndjson (line-delimited events), approvals.json (decision graph), telemetry_window.json (time-series snippets), verifications.sig (signatures and verification metadata), and optional attachments (config diffs, screenshots).

- Incident replay: A UI/CLI feature that reads a bundle or live query and steps through the event timeline with linked approvals and telemetry overlays. Replay is read-only and sandboxed against a synthetic topology.

Functional requirements (high level):

1) Audit schema and event canonicalization:
- All control-plane events we surface must be normalized into a canonical event schema with these top-level keys (flat NDJSON lines): timestamp_iso, event_id, actor_display, actor_id, actor_role, action_type, resource_type, resource_id, change_id, before_snippet, after_snippet, related_approval_id, trace_id, signature_id, origin (control_plane | customer_syslog | operator_agent).
- Events must include enough context (JSON snippets as strings) to reproduce the intent; before/after should be trimmed to a sensible size (<= 8KB per snippet) with a link to the full stored artifact when available.

2) Approval gate record model:
- Approval records are expressed as a directed sequence of decision nodes: request -> reviewer(s) -> decision -> escalation (if any) -> final_state. For the bundle we capture approvals.json as a flattened list of nodes containing: approval_id, change_id, requester, requested_at, reviewers (list), decisions (list of {reviewer, action, at, comment}), final_state, decision_signature_id.
- Approval decisions must be correlated to change_id and to specific event_ids in the audit_log.ndjson.

3) Evidence generation API / Console flow:
- Console: "Export Evidence Bundle" button on the incident timeline. Prompts: incident window (start/end), include customer syslog? include full attachments? retention confirmation.
- API: POST /private/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/evidence-export with body parameters (start_ts, end_ts, include_attachments, requester_role, output_format). Returns signed bundle URL.
- Bundle generation should run with controlled resource limits; for large windows system returns a sampling warning and a compact_mode which picks representative events.

4) Signatures and tamper-evidence:
- Each bundle includes verifications.sig that lists SHA256 digests for each file and a signing envelope (Redwood KMS signature for hosted control-plane; for Private where customer KMS is used the envelope includes both Redwood and customer signatures if available).
- Signature metadata must include signing_key_id, signed_at, signer_role, and an optional notarization chain id (for later proof-of-possession).

5) Replay UI and CLI behaviors:
- Timeline view with play/pause, step to next approval, zoom to telemetry.
- Ability to highlight "anchor events" (approval applied, config pushed, route converged).
- Safe sandbox replay that can annotate topology without interacting with customer infra. Replay must not run any apply logic by default and must warn if a user requests simulation-only apply.

6) Access control & auditability for bundle generation and download:
- Only roles with incident_export permission can generate or download bundles. Generation and download actions are logged as first-class events in the audit_log with event_type=export_evidence and include requester_id and bundle_id.

7) Retention & storage policies:
- Default retention for private deployments: 90 days for regular audit events; evidence export composition allowed for events in retention window. Long-term export for compliance is a customer action; Redwood assists with signed bundles that the customer can store off-site.
- For customers with contractual long-retention needs, define an opt-in policy that stores a minimal index (event digests) + encrypted object references for up to 7 years.

Non-functional requirements:

- Performance: typical bundle generation (<=1000 events, <10 attachments) should complete under 10s; worst-case (10k events) under 120s with a progress indicator.
- Security: bundles are encrypted at rest and transit. When customer KMS is available we encrypt with envelope keys tied to the customer key.
- Scalability: support parallel exports across tenants without affecting baseline inference SLOs; limit concurrent exports per org and throttle automatically.

Telemetry and observability:

- Track metrics: export_request_count, export_success_rate, export_latency_p50/p95, bundle_size_bytes, export_failure_reasons.
- Console must show recent exports and who downloaded them.

Sample incident timeline (illustrative):

- 2025-02-26T11:03:12Z: change_request created (change_id=chg-00027) by alice@cust.com (resource: firewall/rule/54)
- 2025-02-26T11:05:10Z: approval requested -> reviewer=netops@cust.com
- 2025-02-26T11:06:44Z: reviewer approved with comment "allow 10.0.0.0/24 for svc-x" (decision_signature_id=dsig-19)
- 2025-02-26T11:07:01Z: control-plane applied config (event_id=evt-3302)
- 2025-02-26T11:07:22Z: monitoring alert (customer syslog) shows route flap
- 2025-02-26T11:09:30Z: operator escalated rollback (approval chain shows escalation node)
- An export at 11:20 would include approval nodes, the control-plane events, the 6 minute telemetry window centered on apply, and the monitoring snippet.

Packaging and data format details:

- event_manifest.json: small index with bundle_id, incident_id, generated_by, generated_at, event_count, approvals_count, telemetry_windows (list of {start,end,size}), and digest.
- audit_log.ndjson: line-delimited canonical events (see schema above).
- approvals.json: flattened decision graph.
- telemetry_window.json: compressed arrays of timestamp, metric_name, value, source. For packet-level telemetry we only include metadata and a reference to the full object (if allowed).
- verifications.sig: JSON lines (string) containing digest and signature entries; signer metadata.

Operational considerations and edge cases:

- Partial data availability: if customer syslog was intermittent, bundle should surface missing segments explicitly and include a "data_completeness" score.
- Large attachments: attachments > 50MB are excluded unless customer opts in; they are replaced by a pointer and an attachment_summary.txt.
- Cross-tenant joins: disallow generating a single bundle that contains events spanning multiple tenant boundaries; require separate bundles per tenant.

Rollout plan (phases):

- Phase 0 (internal prototype): build exporter that stitches Redwood control-plane events + approvals into a local bundle; CLI-only, internal testing.
- Phase 1 (customer alpha): expose Console export for 3 pilot customers; add signature envelope (Redwood only), retention confirmation, and access controls.
- Phase 2 (KMS + long-retention opt-in): enable customer KMS signing and long-retention index.

Open questions / decisions needed:

- Do we require dual-signature (customer + Redwood) on every bundle for Private? (tradeoff: operational complexity vs customer trust).
- What is a reasonable default retention for evidence bundles vs raw audit events?
- Sampling policy for very large windows (representative vs time-sliced).
- Legal wording needed for long-term notarization or archival in regulated jurisdictions.

Next steps / action items:

- (Jordan) Draft event canonicalization mapping for the top 12 control-plane events and share with Applied ML/Serving teams (due 2025-03-09).
- (Maya) Prototype a proof-of-concept that builds a signed bundle from existing logs (internal) and measure generation latency (due 2025-03-16).
- (Devon) Draft a minimal approvals.json schema and wire it into the approval-service (PR reference TBD).
- (Priya) Reach out to 2 pilot customers to validate retention and export requirements.

Notes & references:
- See linked confluence page for approval gate design (linked in metadata).
- This draft intentionally focuses on investigation and export; rollback and automated remediation are separate workstreams.

Comments / quick brainstorm (notes to self):
- We might want a compact "evidence digest" that is just digests of critical events for extremely long-term archival (cheap).
- Consider letting customers opt to include raw attachments in a separate encrypted object store to avoid big bundles.

End of draft.
